body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 99283bc762978607a1cdba91621e41e6a58ad1ab -->

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is the re-review of the two blocking findings of the 68d58bf head (mkinney's review). Both are closed by a law over the complete input, and the hand-resolved merge keeps both sides.

What looks good

- **Set normalization, once.** `normalize_set` walks the complete ordered set in one pass before any band is cut, each guide after the first judged against its normalized pair-neighbour, and the SAME normalized track bounds both adjacent bands (crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_flow.rs:181-191, crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_flow_set.rs:57-72). The reversal cascades (guide k judged against the normalized guide k-1, never the raw pick) and each normalized track is reused in both bands. The note text still names the shifted chain and the neighbour it was judged against.
- **Ring lap refusal, complete input.** `refuse_ring_lap` checks the COMPLETE single-guide track before a pass is generated (rotary_flow_set.rs:78-100): one axial station AND one radius refuses by name - closed rings and open ring arcs alike - and a guide that advances in station or in radius (a helix, an axial line, a radial arc) passes. This closes the review's probe (56 repeated ring passes) and pins both classes in `bands.rs`.
- **Tests.** The three new pins are the review's own reproductions, run pass by pass and both climb settings. `reversing_only_the_middle_pick_preserves_the_cut_directions` asserts 7 passes with the aligned control beside it; both ring refusals assert the refusal names the guide and the zero-area class.
- **The merge.** The conflict in `crates/app/tests/rotary_flow_band.rs` is resolved keeping both sides: main's `build_with` machine-load side, the PR's `build_at`/`stations` side, with `build` delegating to `build_at` with the default `[2.0, 8.0]` stations. No side was dropped.

Results (local build, this fork PR reviewed locally on the worktree at 99283bc76; no runner - a fork PR cannot use a self-hosted runner)

- Trial merge with origin/main at dc5a34dd1d2e60cadc20abb1523d0f5956f37487: clean (`git merge-tree --write-tree`, exit 0; auto-merge in `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/mod.rs`, no conflicts).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib`: 683 passed, 0 failed, 22 ignored
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test rotary_flow`: 14 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (the heavy-lane rotor twin)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test rotary_flow_band`: 7 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test rotary_flow_lap`: 2 passed, 0 failed (new file, one-line #3187 reason in the body - present)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test rotary_verify`: 10 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

Every step ran in the foreground. The example_catalog suites are not needed: no catalog case exercises Rotary Flow (the diff reaches no catalog file), and the body's claim is consistent with that.

Requested before merge: none.

Notes (not blocking)

- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_flow_set.rs` is now 459 lines, above the ~400-line guidance. The file is the set law, and the split is the codebase's own seam, so it stays. A future pass could lift the meet law (`seg_seg_at`, `clamp_to`, `seg_seg_at`'s interior solve) into the guard module.
- The non-adjacent crossing the earlier review named non-blocking is filed as #4032. It is out of this branch, as the author intends, and the crossing between non-adjacent guides still passes - noted only for the maintainer.
- The new `crates/app/tests/rotary_flow_lap.rs` is a second top-level app test file, which the body's #3187 note covers (two laws, two files, each under the 400-line ceiling). The body links the linked issue with "Fixes #2829". The issue is P7 with effort:high, a new kernel - the label is consistent.
- The body's before/after evidence names the rework gate run on the final head (99283bc76) and the pinning tests; every number it cites matches the local runs above except the app suite counts, which read 7 + 2 (band + lap) locally, the same as the body's rework head.
- The light lane was not run here; it is not required for this PR (a P7, and the review runs the pinning tests).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
